artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a positive integer, and consider the cyclic ring $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$. For a subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$, define the sumset $A+A = \{a+b : a,b \in A\}$ and the productset $A\cdot A = \{ab : a,b \in A\}$ (with operations performed in $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$). For a divisor $d \mid q$, let $\pi_d : \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}/d\mathbb{Z}$ denote the canonical surjection.

Decide whether the following statement is true: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta > 0$ such that, for every sufficiently large integer $q$ and every subset $A \subseteq \mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ satisfying
$$\max\{|A+A|,\; |A\cdot A|\} < q^{\varepsilon}\,|A|,$$
at least one of the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $|A| > q^{1-\delta}$, or
\item there exists a divisor $d \mid q$ with $d > 1$ such that $|\pi_d(A)| \le q^{\delta}$.
\end{enumerate}
artifact.status_search_result: Sum-product theorems in $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ for arbitrary $q$ have been established by Bourgain–Glibichuk–Konyagin and Bourgain–Chang (e.g., the "sum-product theorem in $\mathbb{Z}_q$ with $q$ arbitrary"), giving structural results when $A$ has small sumset and productset and avoids large intersection with subrings/cosets. The precise quantitative statement asked here (with the dichotomy $|A|>q^{1-\delta}$ versus an image of size at most $q^\delta$ in some nontrivial quotient) does not appear to have a definitive published resolution in the form stated; the search did not yield a clear confirmation or refutation.

status_evidence.title: The sum-product theorem in ℤq with q arbitrary
status_evidence.snippet: Sum-product theorem in Z_q for arbitrary q, with structural conclusion when A has bounded sumset and product set, ruling out concentration on subrings/cosets.
status_evidence.claim: Related sum-product theorems in $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ exist but the specific dichotomy in the question is not directly resolved.

status_evidence.title: On sum-product representations in Z_q
status_evidence.snippet: Sum-product representations and structure results for subsets of Z_q.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on sum-product problems in $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$ exists but not a direct answer.
